_about: CONTENT [five side quests played], 11/2/26; CONTENT 2 [ten more], 11/3/26 (ask line 342): fifteen in all, the ten new ones paid by ECONOMY 2's rule (each ending's fx.pay_why says the hours and the rate), three of them met by what is on the map now (a boss's sign: A05, A06; a crew walking home from a raid: A03; a search in a town's lot: D013). Baked by tools/bohemia_side_quests_bake.js from quests/bq (QUESTS' pages, read and never asked to build): every say and every choice VERBATIM from the .bq; the glue (who each role is, where the giver is met on the road, where the second person waits, what an ending pays) is this lane's attempt, draft:true. Played by slices/bohemia_road_events.js: the giver stops you on the road (a face, the .bq's own words); when the talk turns to somebody who is not here, that person's place goes on the map; walk there, they talk; an ending's stage closes it and pays. A modder edits this file, or a .bq and the tool.

dying.name: DOÑA REFUGIO
dying.from: in a chair at the side of the road, a blanket on her knees

wrongdoer.name: EL TUERTO
wrongdoer.from: a one-eyed man at a shack

says: Come close, I don't have the breath to say it twice. There's one thing left and I can't walk it there myself.
There's a man. He took my son from me, years back, in the ugly way. I've carried it so long my hands ache from it.
I want to put it down before I go. I want you to find him and tell him, in my words, that I forgive him. Say it back to me first so I know you have it.

opts.t: I forgive you. I'll carry it.

says: Deserve. You sound like the part of me that stayed angry for nine years.
It isn't for him. It never was. It's so the last thing I set down is lighter than the thing I carried. Go on. Please.

opts.t: And if I change the words on the way?

says: No. He doesn't. That is the point of the word. Cheap forgiveness is just a debt paid on time.
Mine isn't cheap. It cost me nine years. Carry it anyway, or don't, but don't pretend it's small.
Then it isn't my message anymore, it's yours, and you'll answer for yours the way I answered for mine.
I'm trusting a stranger with the last true thing I own. That's what dying makes you do.
Then sit with me a while instead, and don't let me talk you into anything.

opts.t: I changed my mind. I'll go.

says: I know that name. I've waited years for someone to come about that name, and I always thought it would be a knife.
You're telling me she forgives me. Say it again. Say it the way she said it.

opts.t: In her words: she forgives you.
Bring people. Let them see this.
She curses you with her last breath.

says: (he doesn't speak for a long time. when he does it isn't words, it's the sound a man makes when a weight he's carried alone is suddenly shared.)
Nobody will ever know you did this. It doesn't pay. Thank you for doing it anyway.

opts.t: She wanted it lighter. Now it is.

says: You brought a crowd. For this.
I'll say the right things because they're watching, and she'll see it land while she can still see. But you and I both know what you traded to make it a show.
I know that name. I've waited years. Tell me what she wants me to hear.

opts.t: She curses you with her last breath.
No. The truth. She forgives you.

says: (something in him that was trying to open slams shut, and hardens, and will stay hard now.)
Then I'll carry it the rest of my life exactly as heavy as it was. You did that. Not her. You.

10.log: An old woman of the church is dying and wants a message carried before she goes.

20.log: The message is forgiveness. The one she wants to forgive is the one who took her son.

30.log: Carried her words, plain and true, to the man who earned none of them. He wept. Nobody else ever knew.

31.log: Brought them together in front of the whole block. A reconciliation with an audience. She got to see it land.

32.log: Delivered it as a curse instead of a blessing. Loud, in the open. He won't sleep, and neither, later, will I.

33.log: Couldn't carry it. She died with the words still in her mouth. I'll wonder about that for a long time.

says: One course. Two people. I've run the numbers four times hoping they were three people ago.
I'm not asking your opinion. I'm asking you to be the one who says it, because if I say it again this month I'm going to stop being able to.

opts.t: Tell me about both of them.
Is there anywhere else to get more?

says: One is forty, strong lungs, will be back on a roof in nine days with the full course. Nothing else wrong with him.
The other is sixty three, already thin, already tired, and has four people who sit in my doorway every night waiting. With the full course she has a chance. Not a good one. A chance.
The arithmetic says him. The doorway says her. I have both and I can't carry both.
Half each. Everybody wants that one. It sounds like mercy and it's the worst thing in this room.
Half a course knocks a bug down and lets the survivors of it learn you. Both of them get one good week and then it comes back wearing armor, and so does the next one, and the next.

opts.t: Then no. Tell me about both.
Split it anyway. I won't choose.

says: There's one place. There's always one place. He's polite and he's punctual and he has never once raised his voice at me.
If you talk to him, understand you aren't buying medicine. You're selling something, and he gets to name it later.
She sent you. She always sends someone, she has never once come herself, and I have never held that against her.
Full crate. Twelve courses. Tonight, no charge, no interest, no paper.
One day, not soon, somebody knocks and asks the clinic for a small thing. You won't be there. She'll be. That's the price and I'm telling it to you straight, which is more than most people get.

opts.t: Take the crate. Both of them live.
No. We do it with what we have.

says: If I knew, it would be a contract, and contracts are for people who plan to argue.
It'll be small. It always is. That is the craft of it, and you already know that, or you wouldn't have asked.
Say it, then. Out loud, to me, so it's a thing a person decided and not a thing that happened.

opts.t: Not me. Ask the block, in the open.

says: Then that's what we do. It goes in tonight.
Nobody else will ever know there was a second name. That part is mine to carry and I'd rather carry it than have it read aloud.

opts.t: (help her set the line and say nothing)

says: In front of both families. They'll vote like it's a fair thing and go home knowing exactly what they voted for.
It's the honest way and it's the cruelest room I'll ever stand in. Fine. Call them.

10.log: The clinic has one full course left and two people who need it tonight.

20.log: The arithmetic is ugly and simple. A whole course saves one. Half a course saves nobody and teaches the bug.

30.log: Gave the whole course to the one it could actually save. Never told anyone how I picked. I won't forget how I picked.

31.log: Put it to the block, out loud, and let them choose in front of both families. Nobody can say it was done in the dark. Both families heard every word.

32.log: Took the crate. Both of them live, the clinic runs another month, and somewhere a ledger has my name in it waiting for a use.

33.log: Split the course down the middle so neither family could say I chose. They both got a good week. Then it came back, and it came back stronger than it started.

scav.name: LA RATA
scav.from: a scavenger at a stairwell, with a dog

sergeant.name: SARGENTO VEGA
sergeant.from: an old soldier at the bottom of the stairs

says: Second floor and up is spoken for. Something big is holding the landing and it has not eaten in a while.
It doesn't chase. It doesn't bark much. It holds. That's worse, because a thing that holds has a reason.
There's a man up there who stopped moving four days ago, and there's a dog up there who has not accepted that.
I got close enough once to see the collar and the kit. Then it stood up, and I decided I'd seen plenty.
Slow, then. Don't look it in the face and don't put your hand out yet. It isn't angry. It's on duty.
I know whose dog that is. I knew before you told me, because I know who has not checked in.
So there are three ways this goes and I've done all three. I can bring the crew and do it properly, poles and a blanket, and the whole street watches us be competent.
Or somebody with more patience than sense sits on that step and waits it out, which takes hours and works better than anything I own.
Or you make a parade of it, and every person in this valley learns one of mine died alone in a stairwell and lay there four days. Pick.

opts.t: Bring the crew. Do it properly.
How long was he up there alone?

says: Four days. He was two streets from a post with eleven people in it and nobody walked two streets.
Ask me that again in front of my crew and you'll find out what we're actually like. Ask me here and I'll tell you it keeps me up.

opts.t: Then the block should see it.

says: Two hours. Maybe three. No talking, no reaching, and don't take the kit, the kit is what it's guarding.
When it finally eats out of your hand it'll lie down, and that is what will get you, not the smell and not the stairs.

opts.t: (sit down on the step and wait)

says: Poles, blanket, two men, ten minutes. It's clean, it's public, and it's the correct way to do a thing you don't want to feel.
The dog goes to the kennel, gets fed twice a day, and works for somebody else inside a month. That's a good outcome. I want you to notice that I said good and not kind.
Through the middle of the block. In the light. With his dog walking behind him.
Every person out here will look at my uniform differently by tomorrow, and some of them will be right to. Do it if you think it needs doing. Don't do it because it'll look good.

opts.t: No. Quietly. I'll sit with it.

10.log: Something is snarling in a stairwell on the north side and nobody will go past the second floor.

20.log: It's a working dog. Its handler is dead on the landing and it has not left him.

30.log: Sat on the step for two hours saying nothing until it took food out of my hand. Buried him behind the wall. The dog walks with me now.

31.log: Called the crew. Catchpole, blanket, the whole procedure, done properly with people watching. The dog eats every day now and works for somebody again.

32.log: Carried him out through the middle of the block in daylight with the dog behind me, so the whole valley could see how one of theirs ended and how long it took anyone to notice.

33.log: Left it alone. Three days later the stairwell was quiet, the landing was empty, and nobody will tell me which part of that they did.

elder.name: ABUELO CHEMA
elder.from: at a storm tunnel mouth, holding a lamp

says: Every night it comes up the deep. Crying. Sometimes words, and the words are worse than the crying.
The little ones can't sleep. We don't go down that far. You aren't one of us, so you can.
End it. I don't care how. I care that it stops. Don't tell me how.
Water. Old pipe. And below that, further than anyone sane goes, more water and a hum you feel in your teeth.
We don't ask about the hum. We ask about the crying. Go find the crying.
Then you're no use to me and my back hurts from this conversation.
don't shine that at me. i know what i look like now. i know.
they took the half of me that could go home. the other half stayed down here where it's cool and it remembers her.
you have a stick or a wire or a bounty. i can hear it in how you breathe. so do it, or don't, but stop breathing at me.

opts.t: Nobody is doing anything. Talk to me.
The elders paid me to end this.

says: of course they did. I'd pay too, if it cried under my children.

so here is the whole menu. lead me out, which is slow and i might not make it. end me, which is fast and loud and you shouldn't be loud down here. or wall me off and lie, which is the coward's mercy and it works.

opts.t: Come up. Slow. I've got you.
I'm sorry. I'll make it quick.
I'll seal it and say it's gone.

says: you're still here. people aren't usually still here.
there's a way up if a person walks it with me and doesn't let go and doesn't get loud. loud is bad down here. loud is very bad. can you be quiet and stubborn at the same time.

opts.t: Come up. Slow. I've got you.

says: one word at a time. don't look down at the water. look at me. keep looking at me.
there. there's the air. i forgot the air moved. thank you for being quiet. thank you for being stubborn.
okay. okay. do it up here where it isn't so dark, if you can, and be quick, and please don't be loud about it after.
the wall. the coward's mercy. it works, you know. it actually works.
they'll sleep. I'll be quieter. everybody gets a little of what they wanted and nobody has to look at me. go on. build it.

10.log: The tunnel elders will pay to end the crying that comes up the deep every night.

20.log: There is no haunt. It is a person, half-taken, sitting where the deep runs down toward the water.

30.log: Talked them up out of the deep, slow, in the dark, one word at a time. They walked out on their own feet.

31.log: Ended it loud in the deep, for the bounty. The crying stopped. Something far below noticed the noise.

32.log: Sealed the deep tunnel and told the elders it's gone. It isn't gone. It's just quieter now, and walled in.

33.log: Couldn't do any of it. Left the crying where it was. The elders will find someone with a harder stomach.

bq_seed_no_return.title: The Seed That Does Not Come Back

grower.name: DOÑA ANSELMA
grower.from: a seed yard behind a chain fence

trader.name: EL GÜERO
trader.from: a trader with a truck of sacks

says: His sacks will feed this block through winter. I want to say that first because everything after it sounds like I'm pretending it isn't true.
What comes up from his seed doesn't breed. You save it, you plant its children, you get a field of nothing. So you buy again. Every year. Forever, and forever is a long word to sign.
Mine came off my mother's rows. It yields less. It has never once asked me for anything.

opts.t: Then keep yours and take the thin year.
People have to eat this winter.
(wait for her to say the rest)

says: A thin year on purpose. Smaller plates, every house, agreed out loud so nobody thinks they're the only one going short.
That only holds if it's public. A private sacrifice is a rumor by spring and a grudge by summer.
I know. I've counted the block twice this month and I get the same number both times and it isn't enough.
So don't let me be noble at other people's expense. Go talk to him. Just don't come back and tell me his seed is a gift.
Pollen doesn't know about fences. Plant his field next to my line and by autumn my line is his line with a worse yield.
Far side of the ridge, wind off it, and it can be done. It's careful work and careful work is exactly what nobody has time for in a bad year.
Twice the yield. I have never once said otherwise and I have never once had to.
She'll tell you it doesn't breed true. She's right. I sell food, not heirlooms, and a family that starves this winter has no heirloom problem next winter.
Small sack, full load on credit, or nothing, and I'm parked here until dark either way.

opts.t: One small sack. Far side of the ridge.
What happens if the block can't pay?
Your buyers should hear about the second generation.

says: Then we come back in the spring and we're pleasant about it, and there's a conversation about the water rights or the yard or the road.
Nobody gets hurt. Things simply belong to different people afterward, and everybody agreed to it in a year when agreeing was easy.
One sack. Barely worth unhitching for, and it'll get you to spring with a hungry face.
Plant it away from her rows if you're going to be sentimental about her rows. That's honest advice and it costs me a customer next year.

opts.t: No. The block goes thin instead.

says: The full load. Nine years since anybody around here saw a harvest like the one you're about to have.
And next autumn you'll need me, and the autumn after that, and by then it won't feel like a decision anybody made. That isn't a threat. That's just how it goes and you can watch it happen from here.

opts.t: No. One sack, over the ridge.

says: In my own yard. In front of the people who were going to buy from me at the next stop.
Say it and it's true and it's finished for me here. Then think about who brings salt and medicine up this road next season, and whether they'll bother.

opts.t: Say it loud enough for all of them.
(turn to his buyers and say it)
No. One sack, over the ridge.

says: A thin year, signed by every house, or a small sack over the ridge. Those are the only two that leave anything standing in ten years.
If it's the thin year, it happens in the open or not at all.

opts.t: Nothing is signed. Let it lie.

10.log: The farm at the edge is short a winter of food and a caravan is parked in the yard with sacks.

20.log: His seed makes twice the crop and its children make nothing. Hers makes less and makes more of itself forever.

30.log: One small sack for this winter, planted on the far side of the ridge where the pollen can't reach her line. Nobody eats well and nobody loses anything permanent.

31.log: Got the whole block to sign a thin year on purpose. All saved seed, smaller plates, and a line that still belongs to them in ten years. Everybody had to agree out loud, which is why it'll hold.

32.log: Took the full load on credit. Best harvest anyone has seen in nine years, a debt to people who travel, and a saved line the pollen got into. Next year we buy again. So does everyone.

33.log: Told his buyers, standing in his own yard, that the second generation of what he sells is worthless. True, loud, and it cost him the season and me a road.

34.log: Nothing settled, and the planting window closed while everyone was still being reasonable at each other.

keeper.name: DON TEO
keeper.from: at a standpipe spitting air, a line of empty jugs behind him

upstream.name: DOÑA PAZ
upstream.from: at the standpipe up the line, her own jugs half full

says: By noon this pipe is spitting air and by three there is nothing. Third day running.
The block above us is drawing more than their share. I am not guessing, I am telling you.
Go up and look at their standpipe yourself. Then come back and tell me I am wrong.
I do not, not the way you mean. I know what my own pipe does and I know it did not do this last summer.
That is everything I have. Which is why I am asking you to go instead of arguing with me.
Then somebody goes without, and it is either them or it is us, and I would rather it was them.
I am not going to pretend that is a nice thing to want.
Straight up the line. You will hear it before you see it.
You are the third one up here this week and I will tell you what I told them.
Feel it. Ours is worse than yours. Whatever is happening is happening above both of us and neither of us has the reach to go and look at it.
So the only thing left to decide is who gets what is coming down. That is not a lie, that is a valve.
Half a week each and both of us thirsty. That is the honest one and it is nobody's favourite.
Then say it where my people can hear you say it, because they are going to ask me who decided.
You are going to have to walk back down and tell your own people that.

10.log: Hottest week anybody remembers and our standpipe is down to a dribble by noon.

20.log: Walked up the line myself. He was right about the pressure and wrong about why.

30.log: Split it. Neither block gets what it needs and both blocks get through the week.

fx.say: Don Teo sends a boy after you with what the block put in a can.

31.log: Gave it to us and said so out loud. They know who did it and they know why.

fx.say: Your block fills your jugs first. Nobody up the line will look at you.

32.log: Gave it upstream. Our people watched me do it and nobody has said a word to me since.

fx.say: Doña Paz pays you half of what Don Teo would have. Don Teo pays nothing.

33.log: Left the valve where it was. The heat did the choosing instead of me.

kin.name: NIETA LUZ
kin.from: in black, at a house with the curtains shut

witness.name: EL CAMILLERO
witness.from: a stretcher-bearer standing on the slope behind the house

says: He went off the slope behind the house. That is all. He was old and it was dark.
I know what people are going to say and I am asking you not to be one of them.
He wanted to show you something first. He said that to me twice this month and he never said what.

opts.t: What did he want to show me?

says: Dubai. That is all of it. He said the word and he said not yet and then he was going to bed.
There is a box in his room with a lock on it he never explained either. It is yours now, he wrote that down years ago.
Thank you.
Behind the house, past the wire. Mind the loose ground.
You are standing where I was standing.
Look at it. He came off there and landed here, and a man who falls does not land that far out. I have carried enough of them to know.
That is what I have got. I do not know who and I am not going to guess in front of you.

opts.t: You were up here that night.
(look at the ground a long time)

says: I was. I have said so to anybody who asked, which is you.
And if you go down there and say my name, that is the end of me on this block whether I did it or not. You know that.
Then take his box and let them bury him as a man who fell.
At the burial, then, with all of them there, and you had better be ready for what comes after.

10.log: The old man died on the slope behind his own house. Everybody is calling it a fall.

20.log: Went and stood where he landed. It does not add up and I cannot tell you why it does not.

30.log: Kept it to myself. Took the box he left and put it somewhere nobody looks.

fx.say: In the box: cells wrapped in a 2029 newspaper, and a plane ticket to Dubai nobody used.

31.log: Said it at the burial, in front of everybody. That it was not a fall. Nobody argued and nobody agreed.

fx.say: In the box: cells wrapped in a 2029 newspaper, and a plane ticket to Dubai nobody used.

32.log: Told the one person who was up there that night that I know they were up there.

fx.say: In the box: cells wrapped in a 2029 newspaper, and a plane ticket to Dubai nobody used.

33.log: Let it be a fall. The box is still in his house and I have not been back for it.

runner.name: MEMO EL CORREDOR
runner.from: a runner off the {raided} road, out of breath

elder.name: DOÑA FAUSTA
elder.from: with forty people outside the {raided} gate, the {raider} dust still on the road

says: They are gone. One night. I have run that road twice a week for a year and there is nobody on it.
And before you ask: nobody sold them. There was no deal. We were not part of it.
Go and look if you want. I would rather you looked than wondered.
Because we are still here and they are not, and that is the sort of thing people do arithmetic about.
That is what I said.
You will notice I said it without you asking me. Go and look.
Two hours up the road. Take water.
Forty of us. There were three hundred on this ground a week ago.
Somebody let them through and everybody here knows which somebody, and none of us can prove it and none of us is going to try.
What I want to know is whether we can stand on your block or not. That is the only question I have left.
You already know or you would not be asking me in that voice.
Say it out loud on this ground and forty people hear you say it, and then it is a thing that was said and it never stops being said.
Then we come. And somebody is going to have to say whose ground it is, because we will not be guests forever.
Then say it plainly so I can tell them tonight instead of tomorrow.

10.log: An outfit we traded with is gone. Not beaten, gone, in one night.

20.log: Walked their ground. Counted forty and some of them are already on ours.

30.log: Took them in and said the ground is ours now. Everybody heard both halves of that.

fx.say: One of the forty walks with you now. The rest go to your block.

31.log: Took them in and did not say anything about the ground. It will come up later.

fx.say: One of the forty walks with you now. Nobody says whose ground it is. Yet.

32.log: Said out loud who made the deal that let this happen. To their faces, on their ground.

fx.say: The forty give you what they carried out. Somebody runs to tell the {raider} what you said.

33.log: Sent them on. Somebody else's block, somebody else's problem, and I have to live here.

neighbour.name: DOÑA CHAYO
neighbour.from: with a dry hose in her hand

holder.name: THE TAP'S MEN
holder.from: three men sitting on the pump station, rifles across their knees, his tag on the pipe

says: Dry since this morning. All of them, all at once, which is not how a pipe fails.
Word coming down is the pump is broken. That is the word, and I notice nobody has said who looked at it.
It is a walk. It is a long walk. But it is the only way anybody in this valley finds out anything.
Everybody. Which means nobody. It came down the road the way things do and it arrived already true.
It does happen. And every tap on one side of a valley at the same hour does not.
Take water. There is a joke in there and I am too dry for it.
Close enough. That is close enough.
Nothing here is broken and you can see that from where you are standing, so let us not do the part where I pretend.
We turn it back on when we get what we are here for. Or you take it off us. Those are the two.
Less than you think and more than you will want to admit to giving.
Say yes and the taps run by morning and nobody down there ever hears what it cost.
Then bring people and do it in daylight where everybody can see, or bring four and do it tonight.
Tonight is how people get killed over a pump. Yours or mine.

10.log: Every tap on this side of the valley went dry inside an hour. Nobody has said why.

20.log: Walked out to the pump station. It is not broken. There are people on it.

30.log: Took it back with everybody watching. The taps ran that night and the whole valley knows whose doing.

fight.label: THE TAP's men at the pump

win.say: The taps run that night. His tag is still on the pipe, and the pipe runs to his pump house.

lose.say: You got out of it. Nobody pays for that.

31.log: Talked them off it. Cost me something I have not told anybody about. Taps ran by morning.

fx.say: Eight batteries, and nobody down there ever hears it. The pipe still says his name.

32.log: Went at night with four people and no plan worth the name. It worked. It should not have.

win.say: Four of you in the dark and it worked. His tag is on the pipe. It runs to his pump house.

lose.say: You got out of it. Nobody pays for that.

33.log: Came back and said it was broken, same as everybody else was saying. The taps are still dry.

grower.name: DON ISIDRO
grower.from: at a store room of sacks, a pencil behind his ear

hand.name: EL NENE
hand.from: a field hand with an empty sack, by THE POT's flyer on the pole

says: First year this ground has given us more than we eat. First year ever.
And the store is short. I know it is short. I have looked at that room every night of my life for eight months.
I am not going to say a name to you. I am going to ask you to go and count it.

opts.t: You would know if it was.

says: That is exactly the thing I want somebody else's hands on. If I tell you a number you will find that number.
I would. And I have been wrong about this room twice this month and both times I was certain.

opts.t: Then take your own word for it.

says: Door is open. It has always been open, which may be the whole answer.
You are counting.
Then you already know it is short and you already know by how much, so I am not going to stand here and do the other thing.
My family eats what I carry out of here. I am not calling that an excuse. It is the reason.

opts.t: Put it back and we're done.
The block is going to hear this.
Then the door gets a lock.

says: Tonight. All of it. And nobody has to know it was me.
A lock says somebody on this block is a thief without saying which of us.
Half of them will think it is them you meant.
Then say it where they can hear you and be sure, because they have known me fifteen years and they will remember which of us said it.

10.log: First surplus this block has ever had. Somebody says the count is short already.

20.log: Counted it myself. It is short, and it is short by exactly what one person carries.

30.log: Sorted it without a name being said. Store is full, nobody was thrown off the block.

fx.say: It went in a sack to THE POT's kitchen, a meal a day for carrying it. Don Isidro gives you two nights of food.

31.log: Said the number in front of the whole block and put a lock on the door. Everybody watched.

fx.say: A lock on the door. The flyer on the pole says HOT FOOD. ASK FOR THE POT.

32.log: Named them, out loud, in front of people who have known them fifteen years.

fx.say: El Nene says he carried it to THE POT because THE POT feeds the ones who carry. Then he is gone.

33.log: Did not count it. Took his word. The store will be short again next week.

neighbour_one.name: DOÑA SALAZAR
neighbour_one.from: at her side of a broken fence

neighbour_two.name: DON PEÑA
neighbour_two.from: at the other side of the same fence

says: Four posts and the wire off the top of them, between our ground and theirs.
I am not going to shout about it. I am telling you they carried it over there in the night and I am telling you where it is now.
Ask them. They will tell you the opposite in the same voice I am using.

opts.t: Did you see them do it?

says: No. I heard it. And I know what I heard the way you know your own door.
Which is worth nothing to you, and I know that too.

opts.t: Then I'll go look at it.

says: Same reason we needed it. Winter is the same length on both sides of that line.
Go on then. Their door is the one with the good hinge. Ours took the wire.
They already told you. Four posts and the wire. Ours.
I could stand here and be upset at you and it would not make it any more true than it already is.
Or you could go and look at the ground where the posts were. Nobody has looked at the ground.

opts.t: One of you is lying to me.

says: Yes. And you cannot tell which by looking at either of us, so stop looking at us.
Then you have settled it without walking twenty steps, and my house will be the thief on this block forever.
Drag marks. Both directions, one deeper than the other, and the deep one is loaded.
So now you know, and knowing is the easy half.
Back up tonight, nothing said. The one who took it will know that you knew.
Say it in front of both doors then, and say what the ground said and nothing else.
They have to live here after you walk off.
No fence, no fence to argue about. And no line either, which is the part you are not thinking about.

10.log: Two houses on this block. Each one says the other took off the fence. Both are calm about it.

20.log: Heard the second one. Same story, other direction, same certainty. One of them is lying to me.

30.log: Walked the fence. Ground told me which way it went. Fixed it without saying it out loud.

fx.say: Both houses pay you a little, and neither one knows the other did.

31.log: Walked the fence, then said what the ground said, in front of both houses. One of them will not forget it.

fx.say: One house pays you. The other closes its door.

32.log: Took the fence down. No fence, no fence argument. Both houses are furious and both houses are speaking.

fx.say: Nobody pays for a fence that is gone. Doña Salazar gives you half, to make you leave.

33.log: Picked the one I liked better and never went to look. Might have been right. Will never know.

widow.name: DOÑA MERCEDES
widow.from: at the gate of {town}, she watched you come out of the lot

warden.name: THE WARDEN
warden.from: in the east ruins, standing over the dead, waving the birds off

says: You look like you can walk into a bad place and walk back out.
Mine went into the east ruins for cable and did not. Nobody will fetch a body out of there. I cannot pay much.
I cannot go see him like that. But he should not be LEFT there. Nobody should. Will you bring him home?
Forty years a cable man. Could splice anything, mend anything but his own knees.
Hummed when he worked. I keep listening for it. House is too quiet to sleep in.

opts.t: How do you know he is gone?

says: His partner made it back. Said he went down and did not get up, and the one out there would not let him drag him clear.
So he is there. Two weeks. In this heat. I KNOW what that means. Bring me what is left. He gets a grave.
Thank you. Take this. His cloth. Wrap him in it.
He would want to go home in something of ours.
Territory. Held. No taking. Nothing leaves. Nothing.
He will not wake. I kept the birds off him. I keep them all off. Nobody comes for them.
Did somebody come? Did somebody finally come?

opts.t: Somebody came. His wife sent me.

says: Years. Nobody. I stay with all of them because somebody should.

opts.t: His wife sent me. Let me take him home.

says: Home. Yes. Take him home.
Tell her he was not alone. I stayed.
NO TAKING. HELD. HELD.
(He is light. Two weeks and the heat and he is so light. It is a long walk and you take every step of it.)

opts.t: (knock, with the people who came to stand for him)

10.log: A widow at the district edge. Her husband went into the east ruins for cable and did not come back.

20.log: Took her cloth. Somebody is holding that ruin and he has been keeping the birds off the dead.

30.log: Carried him the whole way and brought people to stand for him. She said there will always be a plate for the one who walked.

fx.say: She cannot pay much. She pays it all, and a plate is kept for you.

31.log: Carried him the whole way and handed him over with nobody watching. She said that is how he would have wanted it.

fx.say: She cannot pay much. She pays it all.

32.log: Went through the man holding the ruin to get to the body. Carried him home over somebody who was keeping him safe.

fight.label: the warden of the east ruins

win.say: He fought you for a body that was not his. You carry it home anyway.

lose.say: You got out of it. Nobody pays for that.

33.log: Did not go. He is still out there and she is still asking people.

lineman.name: RUBÉN EL LINIERO
lineman.from: up a pole with a meter, every night at nine

fixer.name: LA FIXER
fixer.from: at a split in the line, a laptop on a cooler

says: Nine at night, every night, and half this block goes brown.
I tested it myself, line's clean, and clean plus browning out means somebody upstream's on my feed drinking before we do.
Somebody still chalks the meter box every month. Never seen who.
So walk it back for me, past the dead storefronts, follow whatever cable's running warm. You any good at quiet?
Because everybody on this block knows my face, man. I've got a kid.
Whoever's drinking that current likes being invisible, and you're new. Nobody comes asking if you don't come back.

opts.t: Who doesn't like being looked at?

says: If I knew, I wouldn't need you, would I? I asked my foreman about it once and he just looked at his hands till I stopped talking.
Follow the split, and don't make a show of it. Please.
Yeah. Fair. I'll go ask somebody else's kid to do it.
Good. Splits somewhere past the dead storefronts, warm cable, you'll feel it before you see it.
Easy. Easy, easy. Don't touch that, it's live.
I don't steal it. I move it. The grid doesn't belong to anybody so there's nothing there to steal, I'm just faster than the meter. That's it.
So. Put it back and go home and nobody hears a thing about it, or make it loud. Which are you?

opts.t: Put it back. Nobody hears it.

says: Huh. That's the one question, isn't it? I don't know whose. Never have.
It runs down, not up. Down, toward the water, and that's where I quit asking. You should quit there too.
I told you nothing, understand me? Put it back or don't. It's your block and it's your face they'll remember.
Light's back. I'm not going to ask how.
You didn't make a show of it, and I noticed. Not going to say anything else about it.
You brought it to us. Could've kept it to yourself and you didn't.
We patch it in daylight, names on the work order, mine first, then the crew, then yours if you want it up there.
You cut it in front of everybody. Somebody's kid was clapping. Nobody's mother was.
They felt that upstream, and somebody up there has your face now. I don't know what else to tell you, man.

10.log: Nine at night, every night, half this block goes brown.

20.log: Line tests clean. Clean and browning out means somebody's on our feed. Found the split.

30.log: Put the current back myself. Block has light tonight. Nobody knows it was me.

fx.say: Rubén pays from his own pocket. He does not ask how.

31.log: Handed the tap to the trades. Daylight patch, every name on the work order.

fx.say: The Trades pay the work order. Your name is on it, third.

32.log: Cut the skim line in front of the whole block. Sparks, a crowd, and somebody upstream has my face now.

fx.say: The block pays you in a can. Somebody upstream has your face now.

33.log: Left it alone. Block goes dark again tonight, same hour.

bq_the_count.title: The Count That Does Not Add

canvasser.name: EL CONTADOR
canvasser.from: a man with a clipboard, going door to door

organizer.name: DOÑA ROSA
organizer.from: at the food line, behind a table of crates

says: Head count. Not names if you'd rather not give names. Just how many sleep on this block.
The food line allocates by count. No count, no crates. That isn't a threat, that's arithmetic.
So. How many.

opts.t: How many, or how many I admit to?

says: Both, usually. I've been doing this eleven months and the second number is always the honest one.
I write a number. The number becomes crates. Crates become a week where nobody here halves a meal.
The number also becomes a page in a room I have never stood in. Both things are true. I'm not going to lie about the second one to sell you the first.
There it is. That question puts a mark beside a block, and I can't unhear it.
I hand it up. Up is a stairwell with no landings I have ever seen. I stopped asking what's at the top, because asking is how you stop being the one who counts.

opts.t: Then I decide what you get.

says: They already came to you. It's on your face.

Here is what the line knows. The crates are real, I've carried them. And twice now a block that gave a full honest count had two polite people knocking a month later, asking after names that were on it.
True number feeds everybody and lists everybody. Short number feeds most and hides the few who can't survive a page. Loud feeds nobody and makes a point. Say it and I'll back it.

opts.t: Short. Leave off the ones who can't be listed.
I read the list on the street first.
Nobody gets counted. Not for food, not for anything.

says: Honest, then. It's the answer that feeds the most people and I still don't feel good handing it up.
If the knock comes, it comes to my door too. That's the only part of this I'm sure is fair.

opts.t: (nod once and let her write it)

says: Short it is. Four fewer crates, and four people who don't exist on paper get to keep not existing.
Everybody on this block eats a little less so that a few of them can stay invisible. Nobody will ever thank you for it, because nobody can be told.
In the open. Every name, out loud, so nobody is on a page they never agreed to.
They'll hear about that upstairs before the sun goes down, and they'll hear it as a block that reads their mail. But not one person here gets listed in the dark.

opts.t: Read it out. All of it.
Wait. Send the true number quietly instead.

says: Then we're a blank space on their page and an empty shelf on mine.
I've watched two blocks do that. Both of them were very proud for about nine days.

opts.t: No. Give them the true number.

10.log: Somebody is going door to door counting how many sleep on this block.

20.log: The count becomes crates. It also becomes a page in a room nobody here has seen.

30.log: Gave the true number, plainly, and let it go up. The block eats. The block is also on a page now.

fx.say: The crates come. Your crew eats from them too.

31.log: Handed up a short number. The ones who can't be on any list stayed off it, and everyone eats a little less for that.

fx.say: Four fewer crates. Your crew eats a little less with everybody.

32.log: Read the page out loud on the street first, every name, so nobody could be listed without knowing they were listed.

fx.say: No crates for a block that reads their mail out loud.

33.log: Nobody got counted. Nobody gets crates either. The block cuts its meals in half and calls it dignity.

watcher.name: DON CIRO
watcher.from: in the street, looking up at a blue sky

tunnel.name: LA FLACA
tunnel.from: at the culvert mouth, people asleep in the dark behind her

says: Look up. Blue, all the way across, and that's exactly the problem.
It's raining hard twenty miles north where nobody lives. All of it comes here. The wash doesn't care that the sun is out over your head.
I have maybe twenty minutes of usefulness left and two bad knees. There are people sleeping in the culvert. Go.
Sure enough that I'm standing in the street telling a stranger instead of sitting down.
Nobody gets a wall of water on the horizon. You get a sound, and by the time you get the sound you're already in it.
Twice. Both times I was wrong I was early, and both times everybody got wet and annoyed and alive.
You want me to be certain. Certainty out here arrives about four minutes after it's useful. Stand there and wait for it if you like.

opts.t: Then I wait for the rain.

says: Culvert mouth, past the dead lot. There will be four or five of them and at least one who won't believe you.
Sun is out. Whatever this is, say it fast, because it usually ends with me carrying my bedroll somewhere worse.
I've heard flood, fire, raid, sweep and inspection. Four of those were somebody wanting this spot.

opts.t: It's raining north. Come up with me now.
Ringing the market bell. Everyone comes.
Then I'm taking the grate off.

says: You came down here. Nobody comes down here.
All right. All right, I'm up. There are two more asleep at the bend and one of them will swing at you before he's awake. Take my hand, don't take his.

opts.t: (haul him up and go back for the others)

says: The bell brings help and it brings shoppers. Half of them will be pulling us out and half will be checking what we left behind.
Ring it anyway. I'd rather be robbed than drowned, and that's a sentence I didn't think I'd say today.

opts.t: No. Quietly. Just you and me and the bend.

says: You're going to open the whole mouth. In daylight. With people watching where we sleep.
Everyone gets out. And everyone learns exactly where the deep goes and who's in it. You can't put a hole back.

opts.t: (say nothing and pull the grate anyway)

10.log: Storm upstream, twenty miles out. Not a drop falling here. The wash is bone dry and the sky over it's blue.

20.log: People are sleeping in the culvert. The water gets there before the sound does.

30.log: Went down myself and walked them out with a hand on each shoulder. It came through eight minutes later. Nobody up top ever knew.

fx.say: The water comes through eight minutes later. La Flaca puts the cells they had in your hand.

31.log: Rang the market bell. Half the block came to help and a few came to see what got left unattended. Everyone in the culvert got out.

fx.say: The market pays for the bell. Somebody took La Flaca's bedroll.

32.log: Broke the grate off the culvert mouth with a crowd watching, screaming into a hole in the ground. They got out. So did everything that lived down there.

fx.say: One of the ones you pulled out walks with you now. He has nowhere to sleep anyway.

33.log: Waited to be sure. It was sunny the whole time, right up until the wash filled. Nobody watched me decide nothing.
